subject: Climate & Environment
title: Fossil Fuel Combustion
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fossil Fuel Combustion.

hook.text: Burning coal, oil, and gas is the single largest source of air pollution worldwide.

buildup.text: Power plants, vehicles, and factories release a cocktail of soot, NO₂, SO₂, and CO₂.

discovery.text: Switching a coal plant to natural gas cuts SO₂ and PM by over 90% immediately.

twist.text: But natural gas still leaks methane, and burning it still produces CO₂ and NO₂.

climax.text: The only combustion with zero air pollution is the one that doesn't happen.

punchline.text: Clean air starts where fossil fuel burning stops.

quiz.question: What is the largest source of air pollution globally?

details.summary: Burning coal, oil, and natural gas for energy is the single largest source of air pollution worldwide. Combustion releases sulfur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, particulate matter, carbon monoxide, and heavy metals into the air simultaneously.
details.whyItMatters: Fossil fuel combustion drives both air pollution deaths and climate change. Transitioning to cleaner energy addresses both crises at once.
takeaways: Coal plants emit SO2, NOx, mercury, and fine particulates
Vehicle engines are the top urban source of NOx and CO
Phasing out fossil fuels cuts air pollution and greenhouse gases together

faq.question: Which fossil fuel causes the most air pollution per unit of energy?
faq.answer: Coal produces the most air pollution per unit of energy. It emits roughly twice the CO2 of natural gas, far more SO2 and mercury, and large quantities of particulate matter and ash during combustion.

faq.question: Can natural gas be considered a clean fuel?
faq.answer: Natural gas burns cleaner than coal or oil, producing less SO2 and particulates, but still emits CO2 and NOx. Methane leaks during extraction and transport add a potent greenhouse gas, undermining its climate advantage.
